previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of severe COPD, diastolic heart failure, diabetes, and morbid obesity was admitted from rehabilitation for altered mental status and hypoxia. She presented with somnolence and respiratory distress, requiring temporary high-flow oxygen. Her condition was attributed to acute on chronic respiratory and heart failure, exacerbated by noncompliance with CPAP. A chest X-ray confirmed pulmonary edema, and she was treated with IV diuretics, with transition to daily torsemide. She developed recurrent right leg cellulitis, prompting a 7-day course of clindamycin and wound care with compression. Despite a documented cefepime allergy, she received a dose in error but did not develop a rash. Urine culture showed Proteus mirabilis colonization, but asymptomatic status precluded treatment. She improved neurologically and respiratory with oxygen weaning, was deemed stable, and discharged to extended care with follow-up arranged for cardiology, pulmonology, and dermatology.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with COPD on 4L O2, dCHF, afib p/w worsening
central-LLQ abdominal pain. Prior hx SBO in ___  // Please evaluate for
evidence of obstruction, incarcerated hernia

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images were obtained from the lung bases to the lesser
trochanters after administration of oral and intravenous contrast.  Coronal
and sagittal reformations were prepared. DLP:  1413 mGy per cm

COMPARISON:  None ___.

FINDINGS: 

CT ABDOMEN:  The lung bases are clear. The visualized portions of the heart
pericardium are normal. The liver enhances homogeneously and there is no focal
liver lesion. The hepatic and portal veins are patent. The gallbladder
contains small stones on series 5, ___ 18.  There is minimal thickening of the
gallbladder fundus on series 5, ___ 19.  This may represent adenomyomatosis. 
, pancreas, spleen, and adrenals are normal. The kidneys enhance symmetrically
and excrete contrast without evidence of hydronephrosis. There is a 4.0 cm
hypodense lesion in the lower pole of the left kidney it measures -3 ___ and is
consistent with a cyst.  The stomach and small bowel are unremarkable. There
is no portacaval, mesenteric and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy. There is no
free air or free fluid.  There are 2 abdominal wall hernias.  The more
proximal of L1 seen on series 5, ___ 44 contains omentum and a small amount of
fluid.  The second more inferior 1 on series 5, ___ 54 contains large bowel,
part of the transverse colon, and small bowel, part of the terminal ileum. 
The small and large bowel loops are of normal caliber and there is no evidence
for obstruction.  Oral contrast is seen past the large bowel that is noted in
the hernia.

CT PELVIS: The appendix is normal. The colon, rectum, urinary bladder and  are
normal. There is no pelvic lymphadenopathy or free fluid.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES: There is no lytic or blastic lesion worrisome for
malignancy.  A calcified granuloma is identified in the right buttock on
series 5, ___ 31.  This is unchanged.  Stable soft tissue densities overlying
the sacrum with calcification.

IMPRESSION:


1. 2 anterior abdominal wall hernias the inferior one containing small and
large bowel.  There is no evidence of obstruction.  The superior one contains
omentum and a small amount of fluid unchanged from prior examination.
2. Cholelithiasis without evidence for cholecystitis
3. Findings consistent with adenomyomatosis of the gallbladder.  This could be
confirmed with ultrasound.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with h/o recurrent RLE cellulitis now
presenting with worse than prior cellulitis, w purulent drainage, c/f fluid
collection // evidence of abscess/fluid collection? RLE

TECHNIQUE:  CT lower extremity runoff from the knee. Bone and soft tissue
windows and axial, sagittal and coronal.

DOSE:  701

COMPARISON:  Lower extremity radiograph dated ___

FINDINGS: 

SOFT TISSUES:  Widespread subcutaneous edema and skin thickening, in keeping
with the patient's known cellulitis.  This is most marked along the anterior
aspect of the mid to distal calf.  No drainable or peripherally enhancing
collections.  No gas within the subcutaneous tissues.  Diffuse atrophy of the
lower extremity musculature.  Grossly Achilles tendon, extensor and flexor
tendons are intact within limitations of CT.  Achilles tendon appears
thickened measuring 9 mm compatible with tendinopathy.

BONES:  No acute fracture or dislocation.  There is periosteal reaction
involving the mid to distal tibial cortex predominantly along its anteromedial
surface.  Some of this appears relatively organized and chronic but there is
some more multiple in superficial periosteal reaction overlying this (series
2, image 131).  There is severe tricompartmental osteoarthritis at the right
knee.  Heterogeneous attenuation in the posterior calcaneus is noted, possibly
a previous bone infarct.


VESSELS:  No visualized thrombus within the femoral vein and popliteal vein. 
Mild atherosclerotic disease of the femoral artery and popliteal arteries.

IMPRESSION: 

Extensive right lower extremity edema in keeping with known cellulitis.  No
abscess or gas within the soft tissue.

Periosteal reaction along the anterior tibial cortex is nonspecific but could
reflect osteomyelitis.

Incidental Achilles tendinopathy.

Heterogeneous appearance of the calcaneus may reflect a previous bone infarct.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  Suggest further assessment with MRI to exclude
osteomyelitis.

NOTIFICATION:  Recommendation above discussed by Dr. ___ with Dr. ___ on
the telephone on ___ at 10:46 AM,  minutes after discovery of the
findings.

(musculoskeletal radiology team consulted at 10:30 on ___ to
report this case).

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with picc  // r picc 52cm iv ping ___  
Contact name: ping, ___: ___     r picc 52cm iv ping ___

IMPRESSION: 

As compared to ___, the patient has received a right PICC line.  The

to lower SVC.  No complications, notably no pneumothorax.  Otherwise unchanged

EXAMINATION:  MR CALF ___ CONTRAST RIGHT

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with RLE cellulitis, CT findings concerning for
osteomyelitis with recommended correlation on MRI  // osteomyelitis of RLE?
cellulitis affects from knee down but osteo looks more distal

TECHNIQUE:  Images of the right calf were performed without the administration
of intravenous contrast at 1.5 T. This study was ended early due to patient
discomfort.  The only sequences performed were sagittal T1, axial T1, and
sagittal STIR.  Motion limits evaluation of all the sequences.

COMPARISON:  CT of the right calf on ___.

FINDINGS: 

Examination is very limited, as it is incomplete as patient was unable to
tolerate the entire exam.

There is a superficial layer of chronic appearing periosteal new bone
formation along the distal anterior tibia.  Limited evaluation on the STIR
images demonstrates possible mild increased STIR signal. There is no
corresponding hypointense T1 signal. There is no increased STIR signal in the
underlying remaining tibia.  There is some overlying soft tissue edema.

In the distal tibia, there is a small area measuring 6 x 11 x 18 mm which is
T1 and T2 hyperintense centrally with a T1 hypointense rim, not definitely
seen on prior CT, consistent with a small bone infarct.  There is subcutaneous
edema mainly at the anterior aspect of the calf.  There is fatty atrophy of
the muscles of the calf.

IMPRESSION: 

Limited evaluation due to motion and ending exam early due to patient
discomfort.

Subcutaneous edema predominantly in the anterior aspect of the calf.

Chronic nonaggressive periosteal new bone formation along the anterior distal
tibia.  Mild associated edema and overlying subcutaneous edema is
demonstrated, may be reactive but early osteomyelitis is not excluded. 
Assessment limited by incomplete exam.  Further evaluation with scintigraphy
suggested.

Small bone infarct in the distal tibia.
